test_name: Term vs charge-off, stratified by grade (mature loans)
null_hypothesis: Common odds ratio of 60 vs 36 months equals 1 within grades
why_selected: Isolates term from grade mix, because 60-month loans skew to lower grades
assumption_check: Breslow-Day-type homogeneity p=3.31e-14: when small, the pooled ratio is an average across differing grades
business_reading: Within the same grade, 60-month loans have about 1.19 times the odds of charge-off, so the term effect is smaller than the raw gap but still material.

null_hypothesis: No linear trend in charge-off rate across ordered DTI bands
why_selected: Bands are ordered, so a trend test is more powerful than an unordered chi-square
assumption_check: Group sizes 6,732-561,904; large-sample normal approximation holds. 'Unknown' excluded
business_reading: Charge-off moves steadily across DTI bands from 14.9% to 30.6%. This is an association, not proof that DTI causes default.

why_selected: Two categorical variables with independent loan outcomes
business_reading: Statistically detectable but practically negligible (V=0.016); rates span only 18.8%-20.6%. Missing employment length (26.9%) separates more than any stated length.

test_name: Income verification vs charge-off, stratified by grade
null_hypothesis: Common odds ratio of verified vs not verified equals 1 within grades
why_selected: Verification is targeted at riskier applicants, so raw comparison is confounded with grade
assumption_check: Large cell counts in every grade stratum
business_reading: Pooled across grades, verified loans carry higher charge-off odds. Verification is not evidence of lower risk here; a plausible explanation is that it targets applicants already considered riskier (selection), which this data cannot confirm.

test_name: Interest rate: Charged Off vs Fully Paid
null_hypothesis: Mean interest rate is equal for both outcomes
test: Welch t-test, with Mann-Whitney on a sample as a robustness check
why_selected: Compares a continuous value between two groups with unequal variances
assumption_check: Rates are not normal, but n is huge so the mean is approximately normal (CLT); Mann-Whitney on 302,715 sampled loans p=0 agrees
business_reading: Charged-off loans carried 3.09 percentage points higher rates on average. Pricing reflects risk ordering, and it also raises the payment burden; the direction of cause cannot be separated here.

null_hypothesis: Recovery-ratio distribution is the same across grades
why_selected: Ratios are heavily zero-inflated and non-normal, so a rank test fits better than ANOVA
assumption_check: Independent samples; 107,007 sampled charged-off loans; 31% have zero recovery
business_reading: Differences across grades are real but tiny, so recovery does not offset the higher charge-off rates of riskier grades.
